draft.title: Seeking Tips on Enhancing Local LLM-Based HTML-to-Markdown Conversion for Complex Sites
draft.body: I've been reading about a project using local LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B/8B with llama.cpp) to convert HTML pages to Markdown offline, aiming to beat traditional tools on tricky sites like SPAs and noisy blogs. The approach involves analyzing site structure with BeautifulSoup, generating extraction strategies via the LLM, and scoring the output for completeness and readability. While it reportedly works well on standard articles (scoring 7-9/10), it struggles with media-heavy or JavaScript-only pages without browser rendering. Also, batch processing speed could be improved beyond the current 10–20 seconds per page on a 4070 GPU. I'm curious if others have experimented with similar offline pipelines and how they handle dynamic content or noisy layouts. Are there practical ways to integrate lightweight rendering or heuristics to better capture media-centric sites? Also, what evaluation methods have you found effective beyond AI scoring to benchmark Markdown extraction quality? Looking forward to hearing your insights or alternative approaches for improving local HTML-to-Markdown extraction.

draft.title: Discussion: Challenges and Strategies for Offline HTML-to-Markdown with Local LLMs
draft.body: A recent project shared on r/LocalLLaMA explores converting HTML web pages to high-quality Markdown using local LLMs fully offline, leveraging models like Qwen2.5-7B/8B on consumer GPUs. The pipeline includes structural analysis with BeautifulSoup to identify content areas and framework fingerprints, then uses the LLM to generate JSON extraction rules and quality scores. While the tool reportedly achieves good to excellent results on typical article pages, it faces challenges with media-heavy or JavaScript-dependent sites without browser rendering. Performance is decent but might not scale well for large batches. Given these limitations, what strategies have you found helpful to improve extraction accuracy or speed in similar offline setups? Is there value in combining local LLMs with partial rendering or other preprocessing? Also, how do you validate extraction quality beyond LLM-based scoring? Sharing experiences could help refine approaches for this niche but useful task.
